artifacts.summary: 4-phase plan landing the cslib-referenced refactor programme durably: committed partition-measurement script, docs/development/PUBLICATION_REFACTOR.md, Proposed ADR-010/ADR-011, full gate; no FormalSystem/ or Tests/ edits.

user_decision.question: How should specs/ (192 tracked task-management files) be handled for publication? The agent workflow commits provenance under specs/ during the nine follow-up refactor tasks, so untracking it at programme Phase 1 would strand those commits.
options: Untrack specs/ (with CLAUDE.md, .claude-extensions.json, .syncprotect, .gitattributes) in one commit at the publication gate, immediately before the v1.0.0 tag
Keep specs/ tracked and published, as the benbrastmckie/cslib fork does
Move specs/ and agent files to a separate non-published branch or remote before publication
user_decision.recommended: Untrack specs/ (with CLAUDE.md, .claude-extensions.json, .syncprotect, .gitattributes) in one commit at the publication gate, immediately before the v1.0.0 tag

memory_candidates.content: In BimodalLogic, any markdown under docs/ or README.md that names a FormalSystem.X.Y module or FormalSystem/X/Y path which does not exist yet fails invariant checks C5 (dotted) and C12 (slash) in scripts/check-module-invariants.sh. When documenting a planned layout, write hypothetical names relative to the library root (Metalogic/Expressiveness/, Metalogic.Expressiveness.Kamp) so the FormalSystem-prefixed regexes do not match; for an unavoidable full slash path use scripts/markdown-slash-path-allowlist.txt (its header names deliberately hypothetical paths as the bar). Never add hypothetical modules to module-invariants-allowlist.txt (namespaces only). Also C9 flags specs/NNN_ paths and 'task N' under scripts/, README.md, FormalSystem/ and lakefile.toml: cite commit SHAs instead.
